note: South Africa's four large card issuers were tried (Standard Bank, FNB, Absa and Nedbank, the four largest banks by the Reserve Bank's own figures and the best-known issuers). Only Nedbank publishes its cards' interest rates, so only Nedbank's cards are written: a card needs its rate, and the other three price each holder individually without publishing a rate. Standard Bank's 2026 credit card pricing guide (fees from 1 January 2026) was read from the bank's own www.standardbank.com copy (its .co.za site refuses this client): it gives a R40 monthly service fee on every card but the Student card (R16) and World Elite, monthly card fees for standalone cards (Gold R24, Titanium R70, Platinum R100, World Citizen R300), a R200 initiation fee and international transaction fees of 2.00% to 2.75%, but no interest rate; its card pages, which say rates run from prime less 0.25% to the National Credit Act's maximum, refused this client. FNB's Aspire pricing guide (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027) gives the standalone Aspire credit card's R35 card fee and R30 credit facility service fee and a 2.75% international purchase fee (at most R125), but its card pages give only a 'personalised' interest rate. Absa's 2026 pricing guide (in effect 1 January 2026) gives its standalone Student, Gold and Premium cards' fees (Gold R39 and R30 a month, Premium R85 and R30, initiation at most R199, 2.50% on foreign transactions) and no interest rate; its rates page publishes rates only for business cards. Nedbank: its rates page (last published 25 September 2026) and its three 2026 fee schedules (Nedbank credit cards, American Express, SAA Voyager; each effective from 1 January 2026) were read in full. Every card Nedbank still sells and publishes a rate for is written: the Nedbank Gold and Platinum, the Private Clients pay-as-you-use card, the American Express Gold and Platinum and the SAA Voyager Gold and Premium, each with its monthly maintenance fee, the credit facility service fee written at its maximum of R69 (each schedule lists a figure by card but says it varies with the holder's risk profile up to R69, and the game doesn't keep a risk profile), its interest rate as the rates page gives it (a range written at its top with its lowest as from), the initiation fee at R219 (the schedules charge R199 for a limit up to R10,000 and R219 above it; the game doesn't keep a limit, so the higher is written; none for the Private Clients card), the 2.75% currency conversion fee (2.5% on the American Express cards) and the R30 fee for a dishonoured payment. The American Express and Voyager schedules charge no late payment fee; the Nedbank schedule names none; no schedule states a minimum payment or over-limit fee. The MiGoals Premium and Private Clients bundle cards come only with a current account bundle and have no rate on the rates page, so aren't written; the cards no longer sold aren't either. The 'up to 55 days' interest-free' is a bank's maximum across statement dates, not a grace period stated for a holder, and isn't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third issuer: Capitec's credit card and fees pages and African Bank's and Investec's card pages answered a Cloudflare check; Discovery Bank's card collection page, rendered, names its Black, Platinum and Gold cards without a rate or fee, its other bank pages answered 404 and its fee guides (including the 2023 ones a search found) answered 500; FNB's card pages answered a Radware captcha and Standard Bank's .co.za pages a 403; Absa's rates and fees page was read again and still publishes rates only for business cards; a search for any of these banks' pre-agreement statements found none, only aggregators' undated figures. So Nedbank stays the only bank written. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: Nedbank's key facts statements for its Gold and Platinum cards give a minimum monthly repayment of 5% of the outstanding balance, and its card pages for the American Express Gold and Platinum and the SAA Voyager Gold and Premium give a minimum repayment of 5% on the outstanding balance; written on those six (the National Credit Act sets no minimum). No minimum payment is published for the Private Clients Pay-as-you-use card; tried: its Private Clients card page (none stated), key facts statements at the addresses the other cards' follow (404), Nedbank's credit card terms and conditions (the minimum is the amount on the statement, with no figure), a search in English, and archive.org's API (a snapshot of the Private Clients page of 9 June 2026; web.archive.org itself is refused by this research's connection).
